Theria.summary: Theria includes the placental and marsupial lineages, together with their extinct relatives. All mammals currently included in Dinozoa belong to this branch.

sources.label: Foley et al. (2023), Science — A genomic timescale for placental mammal evolution
Janis et al. (2020), PeerJ — An eye for a tooth: Thylacosmilus

Eutheria.summary: Eutheria includes placental mammals and extinct relatives outside the placental crown group. Dinozoa leaves the finer placement of Dinocerata unresolved within this broader branch.

sources.label: Halliday et al. — Resolving the relationships of Paleocene placental mammals

Placentalia.summary: Placentalia is the group descended from the common ancestor of living placental mammals. Its major branches include Afrotheria, Xenarthra and Boreoeutheria.

sources.label: Foley et al. (2023), Science — A genomic timescale for placental mammal evolution

Boreoeutheria.summary: Boreoeutheria unites Laurasiatheria and Euarchontoglires. In this game it includes carnivorans, hoofed mammals, whales, primates and rodents.

sources.label: Foley et al. (2023), Science — A genomic timescale for placental mammal evolution

Laurasiatheria.summary: Laurasiatheria is a placental branch that includes carnivorans, odd-toed ungulates and the even-toed ungulate lineage, including whales.

sources.label: Foley et al. (2023), Science — A genomic timescale for placental mammal evolution

Euarchontoglires.summary: Euarchontoglires is a placental branch represented in Dinozoa by primates and rodents. It also includes other living groups that are not in the game.

sources.label: Foley et al. (2023), Science — A genomic timescale for placental mammal evolution

Afrotheria.summary: Afrotheria is a placental branch that includes elephants and their relatives. Dinozoa also places the extinct embrithopod Arsinoitherium within this lineage.

sources.label: Foley et al. (2023), Science — A genomic timescale for placental mammal evolution
Gheerbrant et al. (2018), Current Biology — Early African Fossils Elucidate the Origin of Embrithopod Mammals

Paenungulata.summary: Paenungulata includes the elephant, hyrax and sea-cow lineages. Its extinct relatives include embrithopods such as Arsinoitherium.

sources.label: Gheerbrant et al. (2018), Current Biology — Early African Fossils Elucidate the Origin of Embrithopod Mammals

Metatheria.summary: Metatheria includes marsupials and their extinct relatives. It is broader than Marsupialia: sparassodonts such as Thylacosmilus lie outside the marsupial crown group.

sources.label: Janis et al. (2020), PeerJ — An eye for a tooth: Thylacosmilus

Sparassodonta.summary: Sparassodonta is an extinct lineage of South American metatherians. Its members include Thylacosmilus, which is not a member of crown Marsupialia.

sources.label: Janis et al. (2020), PeerJ — An eye for a tooth: Thylacosmilus

Panperissodactyla.summary: Panperissodactyla links odd-toed ungulates with the extinct South American lineages represented here by Macrauchenia and Toxodon. Ancient protein evidence supports this relationship.

sources.label: Welker et al. (2015), Nature — Ancient proteins resolve the evolutionary history of Darwin’s South American ungulates

Diprotodontia.summary: Diprotodontia is the marsupial group containing kangaroos, wombats, koalas and their relatives. Its extinct members in Dinozoa include Procoptodon, Diprotodon and Thylacoleo.

sources.label: Beck et al. (2020) — Mukupirna and the evolution of Vombatiformes

Vombatiformes.summary: Vombatiformes includes wombats, koalas and extinct relatives. Diprotodon and the marsupial lion Thylacoleo belong to this branch rather than the kangaroo lineage.

sources.label: Beck et al. (2020) — Mukupirna and the evolution of Vombatiformes

Elephantidae.summary: Elephantidae includes living elephants, mammoths and Palaeoloxodon. Mastodons such as Mammut belong to a different proboscidean lineage.

sources.label: Palkopoulou et al. (2018), PNAS — A comprehensive genomic history of extinct and living elephants

Rhinocerotoidea.summary: Rhinocerotoidea includes rhinoceroses and extinct relatives such as Paraceratherium. The giant Paraceratherium is outside the rhinoceros family Rhinocerotidae.

sources.label: Deng et al. (2021), Communications Biology — An Oligocene giant rhino provides insights into Paraceratherium evolution

Rhinocerotidae.summary: Rhinocerotidae is the rhinoceros family. Its extinct members include the woolly rhinoceros Coelodonta and Elasmotherium.

sources.label: Kosintsev et al. (online 2018; issue 2019), Nature Ecology & Evolution — Evolution and extinction of Elasmotherium
Deng et al. (2021), Communications Biology — An Oligocene giant rhino provides insights into Paraceratherium evolution

Cingulata.summary: Cingulata includes armadillos and their extinct relatives, including the heavily armoured glyptodonts. Doedicurus and Glyptodon belong to this branch.

sources.label: Comparative anatomy and phylogeny of armadillos and glyptodonts (2021), Journal of Anatomy

Pilosa.summary: Pilosa is the xenarthran branch containing sloths and anteaters. In Dinozoa it is represented by extinct sloths.

sources.label: Sloth phylogeny study (2022), Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society — Reassessing the phylogeny and divergence times of sloths

Folivora.summary: Folivora includes living tree sloths and extinct ground sloths. Dinozoa includes Megalonyx, Megatherium and Eremotherium from this lineage.

sources.label: Sloth phylogeny study (2022), Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society — Reassessing the phylogeny and divergence times of sloths

Megatheriidae.summary: Megatheriidae is a family of extinct ground sloths. Megatherium and Eremotherium belong here; Megalonyx belongs to a different sloth lineage.

sources.label: Sloth phylogeny study (2022), Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society — Reassessing the phylogeny and divergence times of sloths

Ruminantia.summary: Ruminantia includes the cattle, deer and giraffe lineages. Its representatives in Dinozoa are Bison, Megaloceros and Sivatherium.

sources.label: Ruminant ankle-bone comparative study (2025) — The differentiated impacts and constraints of allometry, phylogeny, and environment

Pelagiceti.summary: Pelagiceti includes basilosaurid whales and the lineage leading to living whales. In Dinozoa it groups Basilosaurus, Dorudon and Livyatan, while excluding the earlier Pakicetus and Ambulocetus branches.

sources.label: Antar et al. (2023) — A diminutive new basilosaurid whale reveals the trajectory of cetacean life histories

Caniformia.summary: Caniformia is the carnivoran branch that includes dogs, bears and their relatives. Dinozoa represents it with canids and bears.

sources.label: Foley et al. (2023), Science — A genomic timescale for placental mammal evolution

Feliformia.summary: Feliformia is the carnivoran branch that includes cats and their relatives. The extinct cats in Dinozoa belong to this branch.

sources.label: Foley et al. (2023), Science — A genomic timescale for placental mammal evolution

Centrosaurinae.summary: Centrosaurinae is one of the two major ceratopsid branches. It includes Centrosaurus, Styracosaurus and Pachyrhinosaurus, distinct from the chasmosaurine lineage containing Triceratops.

sources.label: Madzia et al. (2021), PeerJ — The phylogenetic nomenclature of ornithischian dinosaurs
Chiba et al. (2018; online 2017), Journal of Paleontology — Systematic re-evaluation of Medusaceratops

Chasmosaurinae.summary: Chasmosaurinae is one of the two major ceratopsid branches. Its members include Chasmosaurus, Pentaceratops, Torosaurus and Triceratops.

sources.label: Madzia et al. (2021), PeerJ — The phylogenetic nomenclature of ornithischian dinosaurs

Saurolophinae.summary: Saurolophinae is a major branch of duck-billed dinosaurs. Its members include Edmontosaurus, Maiasaura and Saurolophus, separate from the lambeosaurine lineage.

sources.label: Xing, Mallon & Currie (2017), PLOS ONE — Edmontosaurus regalis and hadrosaurine phylogeny; Fig. 20
Takasaki et al. (2020), PLOS ONE — Re-examination of the Arctic Alaskan hadrosaurine; Table 2

Lambeosaurinae.summary: Lambeosaurinae is the hadrosaur branch that includes Corythosaurus, Lambeosaurus and Parasaurolophus. Many members are known for elaborate hollow skull crests.

sources.label: Prieto-Márquez et al. (2013), PLOS ONE — Diversity, relationships and biogeography of European lambeosaurines
Farke et al. (2013), PeerJ — Ontogeny in Parasaurolophus

Apatosaurinae.summary: Apatosaurinae is a branch of diplodocid sauropods that includes Apatosaurus and Brontosaurus. It is distinct from the diplodocine lineage containing Diplodocus.

sources.label: Tschopp, Mateus & Benson (2015), PeerJ — A specimen-level phylogenetic analysis and taxonomic revision of Diplodocidae

Diplodocinae.summary: Diplodocinae is a branch of diplodocid sauropods. It includes Diplodocus, Barosaurus and their relatives, separate from Apatosaurus and Brontosaurus.

sources.label: Tschopp, Mateus & Benson (2015), PeerJ — A specimen-level phylogenetic analysis and taxonomic revision of Diplodocidae

Albertosaurinae.summary: Albertosaurinae is the tyrannosaurid branch containing Albertosaurus and Gorgosaurus. It is distinct from Tyrannosaurinae, the branch containing Tyrannosaurus.

sources.label: Brusatte & Carr (2016), Scientific Reports — The phylogeny and evolutionary history of tyrannosauroid dinosaurs

Tyrannosaurinae.summary: Tyrannosaurinae includes Tyrannosaurus, Tarbosaurus and their relatives. Relationships among some of its early branches differ between analyses.

sources.label: Brusatte & Carr (2016), Scientific Reports — The phylogeny and evolutionary history of tyrannosauroid dinosaurs
Voris et al. (2025), Nature — A new Mongolian tyrannosauroid and the evolution of Eutyrannosauria

Alioramini.summary: Alioramini is a group of long-snouted tyrannosaurids containing Alioramus and Qianzhousaurus. Their precise position among other tyrannosaurine branches has varied between analyses.

sources.label: Brusatte & Carr (2016), Scientific Reports — The phylogeny and evolutionary history of tyrannosauroid dinosaurs
Voris et al. (2025), Nature — A new Mongolian tyrannosauroid and the evolution of Eutyrannosauria

Proceratosauridae.summary: Proceratosauridae is an early branch of tyrannosauroids. Its members include Guanlong, Proceratosaurus and Yutyrannus, outside the later family Tyrannosauridae.

sources.label: Brusatte & Carr (2016), Scientific Reports — The phylogeny and evolutionary history of tyrannosauroid dinosaurs

Microraptoria.summary: Microraptoria is a branch of dromaeosaurid dinosaurs. Microraptor is its only representative currently included in Dinozoa.

sources.label: Jasinski, Sullivan & Dodson (2020), Scientific Reports — Dineobellator; phylogenetic analysis and Fig. 3

Mosasaurinae.summary: Mosasaurinae is a major branch of mosasaurs. It includes Mosasaurus, Clidastes, Globidens and Prognathodon, separate from the other mosasaur subfamilies represented here.

sources.label: Simões et al. (2017), PLOS ONE — Mosasauroid phylogeny under multiple methods

Tylosaurinae.summary: Tylosaurinae is a mosasaur subfamily. Tylosaurus is its representative in Dinozoa.

sources.label: Simões et al. (2017), PLOS ONE — Mosasauroid phylogeny under multiple methods

Plioplatecarpinae.summary: Plioplatecarpinae is a mosasaur subfamily. Platecarpus is its representative in Dinozoa.

sources.label: Simões et al. (2017), PLOS ONE — Mosasauroid phylogeny under multiple methods

Halisaurinae.summary: Halisaurinae is a mosasaur subfamily. Halisaurus is its representative in Dinozoa.

sources.label: Simões et al. (2017), PLOS ONE — Mosasauroid phylogeny under multiple methods

Elasmosauridae.summary: Elasmosauridae is a family of plesiosaurs that includes Elasmosaurus, Albertonectes, Styxosaurus and Thalassomedon. Cryptoclidus and Plesiosaurus lie outside this family.

sources.label: Otero (2016), PeerJ — Hydralmosaurus reassessed as Styxosaurus; elasmosaurid relationships
Marx et al. (2021), PLOS ONE — Cranial anatomy and relationships of Cardiocorax

Gastornithidae.summary: Gastornithidae includes the extinct flightless bird Gastornis. Despite its large size, Gastornis was not a terror bird of the family Phorusrhacidae.

sources.label: Worthy et al. (2017), Royal Society Open Science — Evolution of giant flightless birds and extinct fowl

Leptoceratopsidae.summary: Leptoceratopsidae is a family of ceratopsian dinosaurs that includes Leptoceratops. It is distinct from Protoceratopsidae and the large horned ceratopsids.

sources.label: Son et al. (2022), PeerJ — A new juvenile Yamaceratops and basal ceratopsian relationships

Rhomaleosauridae.summary: Rhomaleosauridae is a plesiosaur family that includes Rhomaleosaurus. It is distinct from Pliosauridae.

sources.label: Benson, Evans & Druckenmiller (2012), PLOS ONE — Plesiosaurs from the Triassic–Jurassic boundary

Therizinosauria.summary: Therizinosauria is the theropod lineage containing Beipiaosaurus, Alxasaurus and Therizinosaurus. It is broader than the more derived family Therizinosauridae.

sources.label: Liao et al. (2021), PLOS ONE — Postcranial osteology of Beipiaosaurus

Therizinosauroidea.summary: Therizinosauroidea groups Alxasaurus with the more derived therizinosaurids in the classification used here. Beipiaosaurus remains on an earlier therizinosaur branch.

sources.label: Liao et al. (2021), PLOS ONE — Postcranial osteology of Beipiaosaurus

Somphospondyli.summary: Somphospondyli is the sauropod branch that includes titanosaurs and relatives such as Sauroposeidon. Dinozoa places Sauroposeidon here rather than within Brachiosauridae.

sources.label: Mannion, Allain & Moine (2017), PeerJ — Earliest titanosauriform and evolution of Brachiosauridae
